title: International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would give the Cape Town Convention and its aircraft protocol legal effect in Australia, establishing an international framework for aircraft financing interests.
The framework would allow creditors to register interests internationally and use remedies following default, including repossession and aircraft deregistration and export.
The Convention and protocol would prevail over inconsistent Australian laws, with companion legislation adjusting aviation and personal property securities laws to accommodate them.
changes: The scheme would apply in Australia's external territories and have effect for relevant matters occurring overseas.
Rules could give the Civil Aviation Safety Authority functions for recording and exercising aircraft deregistration and export authorisations.
The Minister could prescribe fees and circumstances in which fees were refunded, reduced or waived.
summary.affected: Aircraft financiers, Australian airlines, aircraft equipment manufacturers and the Civil Aviation Safety Authority are affected.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Proposed a supplementary bill making consequential changes to the Air Services Act, Civil Aviation Act and Personal Property Securities Act to support Australia's accession to the Cape Town Convention, preserving Airservices Australia's priority lien over unpaid charges and giving the Civil Aviation Safety Authority a new role recording aircraft deregistration and export authorisations.

speeches.speaker: Warren Truss
speeches.brief: Supported the International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) Bill 2013, noting the convention, in force since 1 March 2006 and ratified by 51 states, would let Australian airlines access a 10 per cent export finance discount under a 2007 OECD agreement, potentially saving as much as $2½ million on an Airbus A380 purchase, and applies to aircraft carrying as few as eight passengers.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Thanked the opposition for supporting the Cape Town Convention bills, which he announced at the Regional Aviation Association of Australia conference on the Sunshine Coast, describing them as part of the government's national aviation policy white paper that would let Australian airlines upgrade more quickly to safer, more fuel-efficient fleets.
